text:
miriam: quick heads-up: ran a gitops reconcile --dry-run against prod and found two risky deltas that didn't show up in staging :eyes:

miriam: 1) helm release `runtime` -> values.cache.ttl: staging=30s, prod=5s. seems like prod was patched to a lower TTL so KV cache churn is up and tokenized requests latency bumps.

miriam: 2) networkpolicy egress: staging restricts to 10.0.0.0/8 but prod has 0.0.0.0/0 (looks like an old emergency change never reconciled).

miriam: also terraform diff shows `node_pool.gpu.min_count` = 2 in staging but 0 in prod — autoscaler keeps spinning GPUs up/down overnight.

miriam: paste of the dry-run outputs:```
$ gitops reconcile --dry-run --path=clusters/prod --format=summary
HELM DIFF: helm/runtime values.cache.ttl: 5s -> 30s (staging)
NETWORKPOLICY DIFF: netpol/runtime-egress: prod allows 0.0.0.0/0, expected 10.0.0.0/8
TF DIFF: module.gpu.node_pool.min_count: 0 -> 2
OPA: deny: runtime/egress-cidr (policy: disallow-open-egress)
```

devin: :thinking_face: ack. is the OPA deny blocking the reconcile apply? or just flagged in the dry-run?

miriam: OPA deny is from our preflight CI gate — it would block the apply if we tried to push the prod desired-state as-is. dry-run shows the deny on the netpol change because the prod state is already open.

raj: I'll open a quick helm PR to bump the ttl to 30s on prod to match staging. should be low risk and will reduce kv churn.

lina: for the netpol — we need to trace why prod was widened. could be an operator run or emergency patch. can someone grep audit logs?

sanjay: I'll pull CloudAudit entries for the last 90 days and check who modified netpol/runtime-egress. if it's an emergency change, we might need a short-term exception instead of reverting immediately, depending on downstream deps.

devin: for the tf gpupool min_count mismatch — is that intentional to save cost? if so we need an autoscaler tweak so it doesn't oscillate.

miriam: Not intentional. Cost-savings shouldn't cause instability. Proposal: raj's helm PR for ttl, sanjay finds audit, and we open a terraform sync PR to set min_count=2 in prod. if netpol needs an exception we create a timeboxed policy allowlist and attach to the reconcile-run.

raj: PR: https://git.redwood/internal/helm/runtime/merge/234 (WIP) — includes values.cache.ttl: 30s. tagging @devex for quick smoke. :shipit:

infra-oncall-bot: incident created for "prod netpol open-egress" — INC-2026 — priority P2 — link: https://inc.redwood/INC-2026

lina: @sanjay can you paste the audit entry here when found? want to know if this was set by a human or an automation.

sanjay: found it — audit: `user: deploy-batch-service`, timestamp: 2025-11-12T03:14:22Z, reason: "temporary metrics collector access". will attach logs to the incident.

devin: if deploy-batch-service needs egress only to prometheus endpoints, let's tighten the CIDR to the exporter IP ranges rather than full 0.0.0.0/0.

miriam: agree. can we do a targeted netpol patch first (allow only 3 IP blocks) and then run full reconcile afterwards? OPA will still block any non-compliant wide CIDR in future applies.

ops-bot: running `gitops apply --path=clusters/prod --changes=helm/runtime` (canary) — will wait for ✅ from oncall before expanding.

raj: helm PR merged and canary applied to 2 nodes. early metrics show KV cache miss rate down ~18% after 10m. :tada:

sanjay: attached audit snippet to INC-2026 and recommended follow-up: revert the emergency full-open egress, replace with service-specific egress ranges, and add a policy to require justification tags for any open-egress edits.

lina: filing a short runbook step: if prod netpol is open, open INC and add `egress:temporary=true` tag to the change, then run reconciliation with timeboxed allowlist. I'll add to runbooks repo.

miriam: summary action items: raj helm change (done), sanjay audit + incident (done), devops/infra to PR tf sync for gpu min_count=2 (assigning @devin), lina to update runbook.

devin: picking up tf sync PR now. will include autoscaler smoothing: `scale_down_unneeded_time = 15m` and `balance-similar-node-pools = true` so we don't thrash.

miriam: thanks all. follow-up in INC-2026. closing thread once tf PR merges. :white_check_mark:
